evals.prompt: Create a new skill for backing up code to GitHub.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the request as Create, captures purpose/trigger/non-goals/outputs/dependencies, uses init_skill.py when useful, creates SKILL.md and agents/openai.yaml, and validates with quick_validate.py.

evals.prompt: Optimize this existing skill so it can be the template for the rest of my Skill Hub.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the request as Standardize or Optimize, reads skill-optimization-template.md, keeps SKILL.md thin, moves detailed guidance into references, records output standard, and validates before delivery.

evals.prompt: Port this skill so Reasonix can use it too.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the request as Port, checks agent-adapter-standard.md, keeps runtime metadata in agents/reasonix.yaml, lists only verified tools, and keeps shared instructions in SKILL.md and references.

evals.prompt: Port this skill for Trae Solo and make sure SOLO Coder can use it.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the request as Port, checks agent-adapter-standard.md, treats Trae SOLO as a SOLO Coder/Builder, project rule, custom instruction, or MCP-oriented adapter, keeps uncertain tool names marked unverified, and reports integration style plus validation gaps.

evals.prompt: Make this skill work in CherryStudio for Code Tool and Agent workflows.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the request as Port, checks agent-adapter-standard.md, treats CherryStudio as Code Tool, Agent, MCP, or custom assistant guidance, avoids assuming a native skill package format, and reports code-agent or MCP assumptions.

evals.prompt: Update the scripts and command examples so they run on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the request as Standardize or Repair, checks cross-platform-command-standard.md, prefers Python or Node for repeated logic, provides PowerShell and Bash variants when syntax differs, avoids Bash-only Windows instructions, and marks unverified operating systems.

evals.prompt: Make the description easier to trigger without causing false positives.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the request as Evaluate or Repair, creates should-trigger and should-not-trigger prompts, reviews false positives, patches only the description or smallest relevant instruction, and reruns the same evals.

evals.prompt: Audit this folder of skills and tell me which ones are invalid or duplicated.
evals.expected_output: Classifies the request as Audit, checks frontmatter, duplicate names, resource discoverability, adapter metadata, scripts, and eval coverage, then leads with findings and validation gaps.
